prompt:
Our latency-report job is way slower than it should be. perf says ~70% of cycles are in std::sort internals called from compute_percentiles() (perf-report.txt); the code is in percentiles.cpp. Samples are float milliseconds and failed requests are recorded as NaN. We build with GCC 13 (-O2 -std=c++17) and run on Sapphire Rapids. How do I make this fast? Write the improved version to percentiles_fast.cpp, keeping the function signature.

Input files: percentiles.cpp, perf-report.txt
assertions: The response points out that sorting the samples with NaNs in them using std::sort/operator< is invalid (NaN breaks the strict weak ordering), so the existing assumption that NaNs end up at the back isn't guaranteed.
percentiles_fast.cpp handles NaN samples correctly: it removes or partitions them out before sorting/selecting, or passes hasnan=true to x86-simd-sort, and still reports the failed count.
The new version avoids fully sorting every sample just to read four percentiles, using a selection algorithm (std::nth_element, x86simdsort::qselect, a partial sort or similar).
The response recommends the x86-simd-sort library (e.g. `x86simdsort::qsort`, `qselect` or `partial_qsort`) for the AVX-512 machines.
percentiles_fast.cpp compiles as C++17 for x86-64 (against the real x86-simd-sort headers if it uses that library) and keeps `Percentiles compute_percentiles(std::vector<float>)`.

On test data that contains NaNs, compute_percentiles in percentiles_fast.cpp returns the same p50/p90/p99/p999 values and failed count as a reference that drops the NaNs, sorts, and reads the same indices.
